Incitement requires a completed crime

questions.explanation: Incitement is punishable only when it is directed to imminent lawless action and likely to produce it. Mere advocacy is protected.

questions.subject: US_GOVERNMENT
questions.topic: Public employee speech and the balance to be struck
questions.stem: A public employee speaks on a matter of public concern; when is it protected?

options.text: All public employee speech is protected
Public employee speech is never protected
When the employee's interest outweighs the government's efficiency interest
Only whistleblowing is protected

questions.explanation: Public employee speech on a matter of public concern is protected when the employee's interest outweighs the government's interest in efficient operations.

questions.subject: US_GOVERNMENT
questions.stem: A state requires a group to disclose members who face harassment; is this valid?

options.text: Only federal groups are protected
The state may always compel disclosure
Disclosure is never required
Compelled disclosure may be invalid if it chills association

questions.explanation: Compelled disclosure of membership can violate associational freedom if it chills membership. The state must show a sufficient interest.

questions.subject: US_GOVERNMENT
questions.topic: Disclosure of contributors to a campaign
questions.stem: Of 12 campaign disclosure rules, 9 are upheld; how many are struck down?

options.text: 9 are struck down
3 are struck down
12 are struck down
No rules are struck down

questions.explanation: 12 minus 9 equals 3. Disclosure of campaign contributors is generally permitted to serve informational interests.

questions.subject: US_GOVERNMENT
questions.learningObjective: Apply the right to receive information
questions.stem: A tank diagram shows a government blocking access to a book; what right is implicated?

options.text: No right to access books
Only the right to speak is protected
The right to receive information and ideas
Only citizens may receive information

questions.explanation: The First Amendment includes a right to receive information and ideas. Blocking access to a book implicates that right.
questions.hint: There is a right to receive information.

questions.subject: US_GOVERNMENT
questions.stem: When may a criminal trial be closed to the public?

answer.exemplar: A criminal trial may be closed only when there is an overriding interest, the closure is narrowly tailored, and no less restrictive alternative exists.

questions.explanation: Closure of a criminal trial requires an overriding interest, narrow tailoring, and no less restrictive alternative. The presumption of openness is strong.

questions.subject: US_GOVERNMENT
questions.topic: The particularity a warrant must have
questions.stem: If 2 of 5 warrants lack particularity, how many are valid?
questions.explanation: Five minus two equals three valid warrants. A warrant must particularly describe the place and items to be seized.

questions.subject: US_GOVERNMENT

stimulus.body: Police tell a suspect that refusing consent will lead to a lengthy detention. The suspect then consents to a search of their vehicle.

questions.stem: A tank log asks whether the consent is voluntary.

options.text: Only physical force invalidates consent
Consent is always voluntary if given
Threats of detention do not affect voluntariness
Consent is involuntary if coerced by threat of detention

questions.explanation: Consent must be voluntary. A threat of detention can render consent involuntary and invalidate the search.
